method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across the power of a single word, the care a speaker owes, the sword of utterance and speech that builds peace, the encouragement of new speakers, teaching as service, letters, ink and poetry, words in public life and publication, the divine Word and its renewal, listening and response, and prayers for a voice offered in service. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. Imported wording checked separately; version differences remain explicit. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.text: He verily speaketh at all times verses that bewilder the minds of the wise, the knowledge of the mystics, and the hearts of the accomplished ones.
selected.reason: Suriy-i-Dam passage that He speaks verses that bewilder the minds of the wise.

selected.text: The wine of divine secrets must be quaffed in holy and intimate gatherings, and the candle of mysteries must be enkindled in the lamp of the pure heart.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the wine of divine secrets is quaffed in intimate gatherings and the candle of mysteries lit in pure hearts.

selected.text: We speak in the Persian tongue so that every soul may find the purpose and perchance partake of a drop from the Kawthar of the All-Merciful's utterance.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh explaining He speaks in Persian so that every soul may grasp the purpose; a choice of language for the hearer.

selected.text: Today the Sun of Certitude hath risen, the Straight Path is manifest, the banners of verses are unfurled, and the standards of guidance are visible.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the Sun of Certitude has risen and the banners of verses are unfurled.

selected.text: You heard with your own ears His life-giving divine call from His purified mouth, and in the Most Holy Court were favored to hear the all-embracing Word
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalling that the reader heard the life-giving call from His purified mouth.

selected.text: so that each may, with eloquent speech and fluent tongue, establish in the gatherings of the world conclusive proofs and evidences of the Most Great Name.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hoping each will establish conclusive proofs in the world’s gatherings with eloquent speech.

selected.text: O Ali! Hearken unto the Voice of the Wronged One and know thou of a certainty that this is that Voice which Moses heard from the Sinai of divine knowledge.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh bidding Ali know that this Voice is the one Moses heard from Sinai.

selected.text: Raise thou a clarion call to high heaven and lift thy voice with a heartfelt cry … Become the confidant of divine mysteries and melodies. Stir up an outcry
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bidding the reader raise a clarion call and lift the voice with a heartfelt cry.

selected.text: The shrill voice of the Most Exalted Pen is raised to such a degree that the tongues of the world and the pens of nations are powerless to make mention of it
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the voice of the Most Exalted Pen surpasses the power of all tongues and pens to mention it.

selected.text: By My life, I remain silent at a time when from My utterance hath flowed the ocean of wisdom and knowledge, and from My tongue the river of mercy and proof.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: I remain silent when oceans of wisdom flow from My utterance.

selected.text: Consider what the All-Merciful has revealed in the Qur'an that you may be assured I speak only what God, the Mighty, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, has spoken.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh asking the reader to consider the Qur’an and be assured He speaks only what God has spoken.

selected.text: Were anyone to ponder what hath flowed from the Pen of the All-Merciful in this wise Remembrance, he would know what none hath known save whom thy Lord willeth
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that one who ponders what flowed from the Pen would know what none has known.

selected.text: they must be nourished at all times from the Kawthar of utterance, that all may appear and become manifest with delicate, radiant leaves and pure, sweet fruits
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that souls must be nourished from the Kawthar of utterance to bear sweet fruits.

selected.text: of God! Your brief letter was detailed, for it was a clear proof of your love. One word that demonstrates the love of God is a detailed book, and one melody raised in praise and glorification of the Loving Lord is a matchless and peerless song
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that a brief letter was detailed because one word showing love of God is a detailed book.

selected.text: whosoever attaineth unto hearing them will behold the world as a handful of dust and the diverse colors of the world will not make him heedless of the Lord of Names
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that whoever attains to hearing the verses will see the world as a handful of dust; opens the section on listening.

selected.text: In the rosebush of inner meanings thou didst raise such a melody with divine accent that thou didst utterly destroy the cawing of crows and the croaking of ravens.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising a melody in the rosebush of inner meanings that silenced the cawing of crows.

selected.text: Today all atoms are observed to be in a state of utmost attraction and excitement, for they have perceived the fragrance of the garment of Joseph of inner meanings.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that all atoms are attracted by the fragrance of the garment of the Joseph of inner meanings.

selected.text: And We beseech Him to cause to flow from thy pen and tongue that which will illumine breasts and open the cities of the hearts of those who have turned towards Him.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh beseeching God that the reader’s pen and tongue illumine breasts and open the cities of hearts.

selected.text: You are shouting although you are silent, but your words will be heard in the future. The words of Christ were not heard until three hundred years after His death
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that one who is silent yet shouting will be heard in the future, as Christ’s words were heard centuries later.

selected.text: One who never attended schools nor witnessed debates, yet with the most exalted call proclaimed and continues to proclaim before the faces of the divines and princes
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh describing One Who never attended schools yet proclaimed before divines and princes.

selected.text: The tongue was created for these days. Beware lest thou restrain it through vain imaginings. Speak forth in praise of thy Lord in such wise as to attract the spirits
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the tongue was created for these days and must not be restrained by vain imaginings.

selected.text: And that is the power of utterance - that thou shouldst open thy tongue and voice, teach the Cause of God, and speak with such eloquence that all women will be amazed
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing the power of utterance as speaking and teaching with an eloquence that amazes all women.

selected.text: Although ordinary sound and melody are merely vibrations of air and physical qualities, nevertheless when they reach the auditory nerve they cause the spirit to stir.
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that sound and melody, though vibrations of air, stir the spirit on reaching the auditory nerve.

selected.text: Thou wilt open thy tongue with the bounty of the All-Merciful in such a way that with wondrous melodies thou wilt cause the people of the Supreme Concourse to cry out
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá promising a tongue whose melodies make the Supreme Concourse cry out.

selected.text: Man must become the interpreter of the heart and the expounder of heavenly revelation. In this state, he speaks in every tongue and truthfully expresses in all languages.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling man to become the interpreter of the heart and expounder of heavenly revelation, speaking truthfully in every tongue.

selected.text: that each one present shall, in great assemblies, with an eloquent tongue and a heart flooded with the love of God, set himself to acclaiming the rise of the Sun of Truth
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: by the sweet-scented breezes of God's love and remain turned toward His horizon. I swear by the Sovereign of all creation that this is a Day wherein not a single letter appeareth except that it is recorded by the Pen of Destiny in the Manifest Book
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that in this Day not a single letter appears but is recorded by the Pen of Destiny.

selected.text: In this material world there is also a material language of the heart. In this material world there is also a material language of the heart and by which the hearts speak.
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on a material language of the heart by which hearts speak.

selected.text: Although writing and speaking can express what is in the heart, the realm of words falls short in fully conveying divine meanings. It is but an indication, an allusion, a sign.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá noting that writing and speaking fall short of fully conveying divine meanings; an early necessary qualification on the reach of words.

selected.text: I hope that you will acquire a tongue of utmost eloquence and fluency and in gatherings and meetings speak in such a way as to bring the attendees to a state of joy and delight
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hoping the reader will speak in gatherings so as to bring the attendees joy and delight.

selected.text: The eloquent tongue is the tongue of consciousness. Praise be to God that that tongue is explaining the real feelings of the hearts and expresses our spiritual susceptibilities.
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the eloquent tongue is the tongue of consciousness expressing the real feelings of the heart.

selected.text: you must manifest in gatherings of the loved ones and meetings of the chosen ones an eloquent tongue, a brilliant proof, evident attraction, fluent speech and elevated utterance
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling for eloquent tongue, brilliant proof and elevated utterance in gatherings of the friends.

selected.text: By God! The hearing ear perceiveth from all things their lamentation and their cry by reason of what hath befallen the Manifestation of the Self of the All-Merciful through sorrows
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the hearing ear perceives the lamentation of all things for the sorrows of the Manifestation.

selected.text: The greatest sword is the tongue. Its authority and sway is over hearts. The sword of steel sheds blood; the sword of speech bestows life. One takes away life; the other grants it.
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the greatest sword is the tongue: the sword of steel sheds blood, the sword of speech bestows life.

selected.text: A kindly tongue is the lodestone of the hearts of men. It is the bread of the spirit, it clotheth the words with meaning, it is the fountain of the light of wisdom and understanding.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Those which strive to speak only that which is truth, which hold the mirror up to truth, are like the sun: they light the world everywhere with truth and their work is imperishable.
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to reporters that newspapers which hold the mirror up to truth are like the sun; opens the section on publication.

selected.text: of mysteries manifest, through Whose revelation the hidden secret and treasured mystery hath been made resplendent! This is the Day of vision, that one may behold, and the Day of hearing, that one may hearken, and the Day of utterance, that one may voice the praise of the Beloved of all
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh calling this the Day of vision, hearing and utterance.

selected.text: I swear by the Sun of the horizon of grace that the drops of the ocean of utterance are more beneficial to the people of the earth than the effulgences of the sun and the spring rains
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that drops from the ocean of utterance are more beneficial than the sun and the spring rains.

selected.text: We have sent down the blessing of proof and the table of utterance from the heaven of grace and bounty. Blessed is he who hath attained unto them, and woe unto every ungrateful denier
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on the table of utterance sent down from the heaven of grace.

selected.text: O concourse of the world! By God, the Most Great Name hath come, which was inscribed by the Most Exalted Pen in every unfurled scroll, every sealed book, and every recorded tablet.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the Most Great Name inscribed in every scroll and book has come.

selected.text: Reflect upon the penetrating influence of the Supreme Pen and the power of the Most Exalted Word. Its traces are manifest from every direction and its fruits evident from every quarter.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh bidding reflection on the penetrating influence of the Supreme Pen, whose traces are manifest everywhere.

selected.text: Open ye the eloquent tongues and utter ye fluent speeches. Sing ye such a melody that while I am in the East I may hear its clear echo and all the Baha'is may become rejoiced and happy.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking the friends to sing such a melody that He may hear its echo in the East.

selected.text: At all times doth the Pen of the All-Merciful counsel those who drink of the wine of utterance to that which is the cause of tranquility for all and the means of exaltation of the Cause.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh counselling those who drink the wine of utterance toward what brings tranquillity to all and exaltation to the Cause.

selected.text: Verily thy letter was received and I was informed of thy chanting the verses of GOD in the Spiritual Assemblies, of thy excellent speech and eloquent address in the illumined gatherings
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá acknowledging a letter reporting the reader’s chanting and eloquent addresses in the gatherings.

selected.text: they would stand and speak in such a way that no one would have any opportunity for denial or objection. Rather, all became enthralled and attracted, and showed the utmost honor and respect
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalling speakers who left no opening for objection and drew honour and respect.

selected.text: Such is His grace that, as thou seest, He speaketh in place of him who hath no tongue, and maketh mention of him - a mention that shall cause souls to be mindful throughout ages and centuries.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that God speaks in place of him who has no tongue; opens the section on finding a voice.

selected.text: Well is it with thy mouth for having drunk the choice wine of utterance, and with thy pen for having moved in remembrance of this Remembered One through Whom the horizons have been illumined.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh blessing a mouth that drank the wine of utterance and a pen that moved in remembrance.

selected.text: and acknowledged His sovereignty that overshadoweth all who are in the heavens and on earth. Say: Cast aside what ye possess and take what ye are bidden by One Who is Mighty, All-Knowing. Thus have We adorned the horizon of utterance with the light of explanation
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh bidding the reader cast aside what he possesses and take what God bids.

selected.text: Thy mission now is this: Travel as much as possible to different parts of America, pass through cities and villages (or towns), guide all to the Beauty of ABHA and raise the call of the Kingdom
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá directing a believer to travel through America and raise the call of the Kingdom; a concrete application.

selected.text: In the course of My journey to America one could witness how, in great assemblages and imposing churches, the spirit of divine assistance would begin to surge upon the utterance of a single word
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalling the surge of divine assistance at a single word in American assemblages and churches; a narrative example.

selected.text: Aid ye your Lord, the God of Mercy, with the sword of understanding.  Keener indeed is it, and more finely tempered, than the sword of utterance, were ye but to reflect upon the words of your Lord
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: They adorn assemblies with eloquent speech and embellish pages with fluent expression. They have kindled the ignited fire of the love of God and become moths consumed by the candle of the Covenant.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing believers who adorn assemblies with eloquent speech and pages with fluent writing, consumed by the love of God.

selected.text: Consider how through their negative words, some can change an eager seeker into one disinterested and indifferent. Yet sometimes, just a single word causes guidance and the awakening of a multitude.
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá contrasting negative words that make a seeker indifferent with a single word that awakens a multitude.

selected.text: Of course, a person sings a joyous song only when he himself is delighted and rapturous. Thus when one begins to guide others and adduces proofs, then his taste becomes sweeter and his heart more joyful.
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that one sings only when joyful, and that guiding others makes one’s heart more joyful.

selected.text: This is a Day wherein the Gate of Utterance hath been unlocked by the Key of My Name, the All-Merciful, and the Ocean of Knowledge hath surged before the faces of all who are in the heavens and on earth.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the Gate of Utterance has been unlocked by the Key of the Name, the All-Merciful.

selected.text: the people by their inward, spiritual qualities. Let no one raise his tongue in intentional or unintentional malice against his brother or sister. We must watch our tongues. This Cause is very great and the circle of our patience must be very wide. Let every man write this sentence 'Watch thy tongue' on the tablet of his heart
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in Paris urging everyone to write “Watch thy tongue” on the tablet of the heart; a memorable practical injunction against malicious speech.

selected.text: By the Most Great Luminary! His utterance transcendeth the utterance of the peoples of the world, His mention surpasseth the mention of all nations, and His movement and stillness are distinct from all else.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that His utterance transcends the utterance of the peoples of the world; marks the difference from ordinary eloquence.

selected.text: The Blessed Perfection often remarked that a lecture must be like unto a cool, pure, refreshing stream of water. It is not necessary to use dark, obsolete and difficult words; the simpler the more effective.
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalling that a lecture should be like a cool, pure stream and that simpler words are more effective; supplies the flowing-water image.

selected.text: Every bird which reaches the rose garden breaks forth into lay and begins singing various harmonies. It is inspired with wonderful melodies and heart-rejoicing songs. It stirs into cheerfulness the listeners.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that every bird reaching the rose garden sings and cheers its listeners.

selected.text: These very conversations of ours today consisted of the spiritual food. God had so destined that you (Mrs Fraser) be here with us in this train so that undisturbed we may talk together on these ideal subjects.
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that their conversation on the train was spiritual food; an everyday conversation as an occasion of service.

selected.text: In those dense woods may they raise such a roar that it will cause the hearts of the veiled ones to tremble and leave the jackals of ignorance and unawareness no choice but to flee. That roar is the divine call
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hoping for a roar, the divine call, that makes the veiled tremble and the jackals of ignorance flee.

selected.text: The reason for this servant's mention of the end is not clear, for the verses have not ended and the evidences have not accepted conclusion. In the nights and days verses are being revealed like the pouring rain
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the verses have not ended but are revealed like pouring rain.

selected.text: O people of the graves! By God! The trumpet hath been sounded and the mountains have passed away and the heaven hath come with a manifest command. Arise and turn with shining faces toward the Supreme Horizon.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh addressing the people of the graves: the trumpet has been sounded.

selected.text: A thousand times it was written that the interference of the clergy in political matters would result in calamities … with such clear language were warning and counsel given, but ears were deaf and eyes were blind
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalling warnings given in clear language to which ears were deaf; shows that eloquence does not always persuade.

selected.text: One pure deed and one goodly attribute hath guided and will continue to guide multitudes. In ancient times, a person known as Hanzala, through one word spoken with sincerity, guided a king and many of his subjects.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh recalling Hanzala, who guided a king and his subjects through one sincere word; a narrative example of speech and deed.

selected.text: In truth, the living waters of human utterance have ever been and shall remain the fountain of life, for they revive withered forms and quicken those who lie dead in the wilderness of heedlessness and forgetfulness.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the living waters of human utterance revive withered forms and quicken the heedless.

selected.text: Grant me a serene heart, an expanded breast, a joyful spirit, an enlivened mind, a watchful eye, a radiant countenance, an awakened vision, an eloquent tongue, penetrating thought, powerful speech and clear expression.
selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá for a serene heart, eloquent tongue and clear expression; joins speech to inner qualities.

selected.text: O Lord! Assist them with the army of proofs and evidences, confirm them with wisdom and understanding and inspire their tongues with such eloquence and elucidation as to humble the intelligences and conquer the voices!
selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking that tongues be inspired with eloquence, wisdom and proofs.

selected.text: The water of utterance hath a penetrating power and influence which most of the people of the world are powerless to comprehend. This is that water concerning which He saith: "And from water We made every living thing."
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the water of utterance has a penetrating power few comprehend, “from water We made every living thing.”

selected.text: Through the movement of the Most Exalted Pen a new spirit of inner meanings was breathed by the command of the True Commander into the bodies of words, and its effects are visible and manifest in all things of the world.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the Most Exalted Pen breathed a new spirit of meanings into the bodies of words.

selected.text: Speech is of two kinds: one is comprehensive utterances and decisive speech which is extremely concise yet meaningful; the other is legends and stories which are verbose, lengthy and prolix but with few and rare meanings.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá distinguishing concise, meaningful speech from verbose stories with few meanings; a measure of substance over length.

selected.text: A word spoken by the tongue for the Cause of God is like the Most Great Luminary - though clouds and mists may temporarily veil it, ere long it will emerge from behind the clouds and illumine the world with its effulgence.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh likening a word spoken for the Cause to the sun that emerges from behind clouds.

selected.text: when mention of the divine friends flows from the tongue or the pen inscribes their names, such a state occurs that pen and paper are moved to ecstasy and delight, and the ink cries out "May my soul be sacrificed for them!"
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in which pen, paper and ink are moved to ecstasy when the names of the friends are written.

selected.text: By the life of God, the fortresses of hearts - their stones scatter, their rocks disintegrate, their foundations are uprooted by your sharp sword of utterance, and their gates are opened by your maces from which sparks fly.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá picturing the fortresses of hearts opened by the sharp sword of utterance; a vivid image of persuasive speech.

selected.text: The man answered: 'The proof of Muhammad was His eloquent Arabic book. I have heard that this young man has brought through revelation several eloquent Arabic and Persian epistles which have the spirit of the word of Muhammad.'
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in which a man cites eloquent Arabic and Persian epistles as proof; a narrative on eloquence as evidence.

selected.text: Be thou occupied with the mention of the Truth through wisdom and utterance, that perchance the dead may attain unto life through the sweet-scented breezes of the garment of the All-Merciful, and the withered may be made fresh.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh to be occupied with wisdom and utterance that the dead may attain life and the withered be refreshed.

selected.text: Therefore, open your tongue to these mysteries and proclaim the outpourings of this luminous century. Sometimes string together pearls of poetry, and sometimes make manifest through prose the meanings of this Day of Manifestation
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bidding the reader sometimes string pearls of poetry and sometimes make meanings manifest through prose.

selected.text: The article that was published in the St. Petersburg newspaper was in the utmost eloquence and excellence, and it was evidence of your outstanding services. Such beneficial articles are the cause of the spread of the divine call.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising an eloquent article in a St. Petersburg newspaper as a cause of spreading the divine call.

selected.text: Some breezes refresh the body like the spring breeze and some hurt the body. Some words lighten the heart and others crush it. The breeze of the Disciples quickened the spirit and the words of the Pharisees deadened and killed it.
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá comparing words to breezes that refresh or hurt, contrasting the Disciples’ quickening breeze with the Pharisees’ deadening words.

selected.text: O Lord! Cause his tongue to speak with utterance, adorn his heart with the verses of exposition, and make his breaths to be confirmed by the breath of the All-Merciful, that he may loose his tongue in the field of divine knowledge
selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that a soul’s tongue speak with utterance and his heart be adorned with exposition.

selected.text: This Day is the Day whose mention hath flowed from the Pen and been recorded in the Books of the past and of the future. Blessed is he who hath turned unto it, and drunk, and attained, and woe to the heedless, and woe to the deniers.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that this Day was recorded in the Books of past and future.

selected.text: The voice of the physical clarion may travel the distance of three miles, but the harmony of the spiritual Clarion reacheth to the East and the West. The effect of that is only in the bodies; but the effect of this is in the spirits.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá contrasting the three-mile reach of the physical clarion with the spiritual clarion heard East and West.

selected.text: words have acquired the power of meanings, and expressions have become the truth of allusions and glad tidings of abstract meanings. A word has taken on the quality of a book, and a letter has found the station of a decisive utterance.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that words have acquired the power of meanings, a word the quality of a book.

selected.text: Today those souls who are free from every thought save the True One, their hearts are inspired with the divine inspiration. Whenever they begin to speak on any subject they are prompted by the spirit, as though some one speaks to them.
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that souls free from all thought save God speak as though prompted by the spirit.

selected.text: O Exalted Pen! Make mention of those whom We have related to thy exalted Self, and mention them with such remembrances as will cause the fish in the seas to be attracted, the fruits upon the trees and the birds in their nests to speak.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh bidding the Pen mention the friends in such wise that fish, fruits and birds would speak.

selected.text: I swear by the Most Great Name that the tongue was created for the remembrance of God - if it attaineth not thereunto it is assuredly severed - and the ears were created to hearken unto His words, and likewise all the limbs and members.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the tongue was created for the remembrance of God and the ears to hearken to His words.

selected.text: The water of life is the divine utterance, and likewise His clear evidences. Strive that perchance the people of the world may attain eternal life through this everlasting stream and may illumine creation with the light of wisdom
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the water of life is the divine utterance, through which the world may attain eternal life.

selected.text: I beseech Thee by the Name through Whose manifestation both the kingdom of earth and heaven were attracted, livers and hearts were melted, the ocean of utterance surged in the realm of possibility, and the nightingale sang upon the branches
selected.reason: Prayer of Bahá’u’lláh by the Name through which the ocean of utterance surged and the nightingale sang.

selected.text: O servants! Turn your eyes from these matters and purify your hearts, for today such bounty has appeared that in a single day and night, if a scribe were capable, the equivalent of the Persian Bayan could be revealed from the holy divine heaven.
selected.reason: Lawh-i-Sarraj passage that in a single day and night the equivalent of the Persian Bayan could be revealed; conveys the abundance of revelation.

selected.text: Hassan Khargain. This orator had a son who had studied philosophy and sciences and considered himself secretly greater than his father. He marvelled at the simple words of his father, playing such wonderful effect upon the hearts of his hearers.
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in Budapest introducing the orator whose philosophically trained son marvelled at the effect of his father’s simple words; a narrative example.

selected.text: Without helper or assistant He summoned the peoples of the world to the horizon of the Most Great Name. That call became a fire of hatred in the hearts of the idolaters, and the choice sealed wine in the hearts of those who are near and sincere.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that His call became hatred in the idolaters and choice wine in the sincere; the Word’s different reception.

selected.text: When thou dost win to My Tablet and find the fragrance of revelation in My utterance, say: My God, my God! Praise be to Thee for showing me Thy signs, causing me to hear the shrill voice of Thy Pen, and illumining my heart with the light of Thy knowledge
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh teaching the reader a prayer of thanks on finding the fragrance of revelation in His utterance; a response to the Word.

selected.text: The one God adorned man with the ornament of utterance, and this utterance is special to him and through it man is distinguished from animal. In the Furqan, which distinguishes between truth and falsehood, He says: "He created man, taught him utterance."
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that God adorned man with utterance, distinguishing him from the animal, citing “He created man, taught him utterance.”

selected.text: They must be eloquent speakers and heralds, and in the utmost joy and gladness, recite the verses of guidance and interpret the words sent down from the heaven of praise and glorification, sending their exaltation and sanctification to the Supreme Kingdom.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking that the friends be eloquent heralds who recite and interpret the verses with joy.

selected.text: By God's life! They know not what issueth from their mouths. These are but worthless followers who pursue their desires on a Day whereon the Herald hath called out from the Most Exalted Horizon: "O people of creation! The Throne hath been established in Akka
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on followers who know not what issues from their mouths while the Herald proclaims from the Most Exalted Horizon.

selected.text: No sword is sharper than the Word of God. If a few souls arise purely for the sake of God, speak for God and fix their gaze upon God, assuredly its effects will become manifest and evident in the world, as indeed they have become manifest and ye witness them.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that no sword is sharper than the Word of God when a few souls speak purely for God.

selected.text: Be thou vocal with that which will cause the spirit of the world to soar and the hearts of them who are nigh to be attracted. Warble upon the branches of the Divine Lote-Tree with diverse melodies that the followers of all religions may be set ablaze thereby.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh bidding the believer be vocal so that the followers of all religions may be set ablaze.

selected.text: Therefore, take up the eloquent pen and inscribe upon the simple tablet the essence of expression and rhetoric, so that you may fulfill the right of fluency, eloquence and sweetness of expression, and demonstrate the miracle of divine rhetoric and expression.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bidding a writer take up the eloquent pen and demonstrate the miracle of divine rhetoric; bridges speech and writing.

selected.text: At one time I hear thy melodies, and at another thy sighing and weeping. It is as though patience hath been severed from thee at dawn when I hear thy lamentations, at eventide thy crying, and at daybreak that which hath caused the hearts of the mystics to burn.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh describing the melodies, sighs and laments heard from a soul at dawn and eventide.

selected.text: Draw forth the sword of the tongue from the scabbard of utterance through the power of the All-Merciful, and proclaim this Cause in such wise that no created thing shall find means to turn away, for these loved ones are aided by the Holy Spirit when they speak.
selected.reason: Lawh-i-Javad passage bidding the friends draw the sword of the tongue and proclaim the Cause, aided by the Holy Spirit when they speak.

selected.text: I beseech Thee, O Lord of existence, by Thy Command whereby the ocean of utterance surged in contingent being and the dove of understanding warbled upon the branches, to enable me to serve Thy Cause in such wise that my remembrance may influence hearts and minds.
selected.reason: Prayer of Bahá’u’lláh to serve the Cause so that one’s remembrance may influence hearts and minds.

selected.text: she will become the possessor of a fluent speech and will find her heart brilliant and full of serenity and faith to such an extent that her pure breath will so take effect even in stone, tree and clay (i.e., in all people), that she, herself, will be astonished.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá promising that she will gain fluent speech and a heart so serene that her breath affects even stone, tree and clay.

selected.text: be purified and sanctified through the water of the All-Merciful's utterance and become occupied with teaching the Cause. This is a station which the pen is powerless to describe and understanding faileth to comprehend. The words of holy souls are so effective and penetrating that they can make a withered tree fresh and adorned with delicate, precious fruits
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the words of holy souls can make a withered tree fresh and fruitful.

selected.text: Come forth from behind the veil of silence, then loose thy tongue in praise of thy Lord, that thou mayest be among those who are guided, and remind people through thy remembrance, that perchance through thee may be brought about in them what God hath chosen for them.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh bidding the reader come forth from behind the veil of silence and loose the tongue in praise.

selected.text: The tongue is the dawning-place of the lights of truth; make it not the source of false utterances. The tongue is the treasury of My praise and mention; occupy it not with the remembrance of this one and that one, for it shall be a sign unto itself in its own station.
selected.reason: Kitab-i-Badi’ passage calling the tongue the dawning-place of the lights of truth, not a source of falsehood; a foundational statement on truthful speech.

selected.text: He is God, exalted be His glory, the Most Great! … Praise be to God Who hath spoken that whereby all things were attracted, and through Whom His path and His balance were made manifest, and whatsoever was recorded in the Books, the Scriptures, the Psalms and the Tablets
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh praising God Who spoke that whereby all things were attracted and His balance made manifest.

selected.text: thy melody must rise high and thy song and voice bring the Concourse on High to ecstasy and joy. … The rest is up to you, for the breath of the spirit was blown into thee and a ray from the Abha Kingdom fell upon thy heart. Given this, silence and quietude are not permitted
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that once the breath of the spirit has entered the heart, silence and quietude are not permitted.

selected.text: This is the Day of remembrance and utterance, the Day of assistance and service. All must remain firm and steadfast in the Cause of the Lord of creation in complete unity. The triumph of God's Cause hath been and shall be through goodly deeds and firm, decisive utterances.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the triumph of the Cause is through goodly deeds and decisive utterances in unity.

selected.text: He was established upon the throne of utterance and with the most exalted call summoned the peoples of earth and heaven to the supreme horizon. By the sword of wisdom and utterance, the hearts and minds of the peoples of the world have been and shall continue to be opened.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that by the sword of wisdom and utterance the hearts of the world are opened.

selected.text: But when a man ariseth to expound the arguments of God and invite people to enter in the religion of God, and when he uttereth those arguments and advanceth consummate proofs concerning the appearance of the great Kingdom, then intense love shall become manifest in his heart.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that intense love becomes manifest in the heart of one who arises to expound the proofs of God.

selected.text: Speech is from His special grace and the pen from His infinite bounty. The connection of the world, the fellowship and gathering of nations, and all stations and ranks are made manifest through these two. They are two mighty interpreters that He has bestowed upon His servants.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh calling speech and the pen two mighty interpreters through which the fellowship of nations is made manifest.

selected.text: "In movements there is life, in immobility there is death. The traveling of the teachers from place to place, from Orient to Occident, and from country to country, is one of the greatest means for spreading the Fragrances, and for sowing spiritual seeds in the souls of the people."
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that in movement there is life, and that teachers’ travel is a great means of sowing spiritual seeds.

selected.text: One goodly word uttered with sincerity is more beloved in the sight of God than a hundred thousand swords raised in His Name, for in this Revelation the ocean of mercy is surging, the sun of bounty is shining, and all are forbidden from that which causeth injury, fear, and distress.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that one sincere goodly word is more beloved than a hundred thousand swords, since all are forbidden what causes injury.

selected.text: Therefore, a letter in fine handwriting by a skilled calligrapher bears no fruit unless it contains pleasing meanings and sweet contents. The sweetness of expression lies in the delicacy of meanings and indication of spiritual love, conscientious attractions, and merciful sentiments
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that fine calligraphy bears no fruit without pleasing meanings and spiritual love; the guide’s test of outward polish.

selected.text: I cannot describe the eloquent contents and fluent expressions of your noble letter, and I cannot express the sweetness, fluidity, excellence and delicacy of the mysteries and meanings of your poetry. How excellent is the one who said "And when you speak, you are indeed the Gemini."
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising the eloquence of a letter and the delicacy of its poetry; carries the guide’s attention to poetry.

selected.text: Nevertheless, the Most Exalted Pen hath not been prevented from mention and praise, and night and day summoneth the peoples of the earth to the Most Exalted Horizon. No authority hath restrained Him and no fear hath seized Him. He hath spoken and continueth to speak before all faces
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that despite all hindrance the Most Exalted Pen has continued to speak before all faces.

selected.text: O friends! Know ye your worth and withhold not yourselves from that which is with God. Each one of you must be even as the morning star, radiant, that souls who have strayed in the darkness of idle fancies and selfish desires may thereby be guided and find the path of deliverance.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh bidding the friends know their worth and be radiant as the morning star to guide the strayed.

selected.text: The Word of God is like the promise-laden winds of spring and when this word can pass through spiritual lips it grants the breath of life indeed and imparts spiritual salvation. It transforms the pure earth into a rose garden and fills the horizon of existence with the fragrance of musk.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá likening the Word of God through spiritual lips to the promise-laden winds of spring.

selected.text: It is very good that thy breath is very effective. No matter with whomsoever thou speakest about the cause he will be impressed and accept the revelation. This is because thou art seeking the good-pleasure of the Lord. Thou art not serving the Cause for fame but to be drawn near unto God.
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to Stanwood Cobb that his breath is effective because he seeks God’s good-pleasure rather than fame.

selected.text: O people! The breathings of the words of the Lord of Names and Attributes have so seized me that the veils have been rent asunder by the fingers of the power of Him Who is the Fashioner of the heavens and earth, and I have turned toward the countenance whereby the worlds have been illumined.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh describing being seized by the breathings of the words of the Lord.

selected.text: If a lover holds the hand of a beloved, it is obvious what feelings ensue. They communicate face to face and speak heart to heart, as this light is communicating now with human eyes, the sun with the earth, the cloud with the land and the breeze with the tree. This process is found in all things.
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on communication heart to heart, as light with the eye and the breeze with the tree.

selected.text: Utterance is a substance that seeketh penetration and moderation. As to penetration, it is conditional upon refinement, which in turn is dependent upon hearts that are detached and pure. As for moderation, it is to be combined with wisdom, which We have revealed in the Scriptures and Tablets.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that utterance seeketh penetration and moderation, dependent on pure hearts and on wisdom; the fullest of the guide’s several versions of this principle.

selected.text: All these have in themselves an organization, and are constructed on natural law. Therefore, they correspond to the order of existence like something which would fit into a mold. A true voice fits into the mold of nature. When it is so, this affects the nerves, and they affect the heart and spirit.
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that a true voice fits the mould of nature and so affects the nerves, heart and spirit.

selected.text: If in certain instances heedlessness hath occurred, verily He hath forgiven what is past. God willing, arise henceforth to make good what hath escaped you. … The world is not worthy of mention, and its evanescence is witnessed at every moment. Arise to serve the Cause of God with wisdom and utterance
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh assuring forgiveness of past heedlessness and bidding the reader arise to serve the Cause with wisdom and utterance.

selected.text: We thank Him for having caused you to speak His praise and enabled you to set forth His proof and establish His arguments and evidences and manifest His Cause throughout His creation. Were people to possess attentive ears, pure minds, assured souls and clear hearts, this treatise would suffice them.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá giving thanks that a writer set forth God’s proofs, noting that attentive ears and pure hearts would find his treatise sufficient.

selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh replying to a handmaiden out of love for God even when sorrow had stilled the pen; letters written amid hardship.

selected.text: Today whosoever takes the lessons of voice culture in the Celestial Conservatory of Baha'u'llah, he will be endowed with a soul-captivating voice which would move and thrill the hearts of numberless music lovers
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that one who studies voice culture in the Celestial Conservatory of Bahá’u’lláh will move numberless hearts.

selected.text: I have taken up the pen and engaged in mentioning that yearner for the Beauty of the All-Merciful, that perhaps from the effect of this pen and ink a sweet fragrance may reach the nostrils of the hearts of the people of love, and hearts and breasts may become expanded and gladdened through divine remembrance.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá taking up the pen in the hope that pen and ink may carry a sweet fragrance to loving hearts.

selected.text: By God! There hath appeared what hath never appeared in the world, and the Speaker of Sinai hath spoken that which, were it to be cast upon the mountains, they would take flight, and were it cast upon the earth, its treasures would be revealed, and were it cast upon the heaven, it would be cleft asunder instantly.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the Speaker of Sinai has spoken words that would make mountains take flight.

selected.text: We counsel all to assist the Cause of God through the hosts of deeds and character. Any deed performed by any soul for the sake of God that becomes the cause of guiding others is worthy to be recorded and, by the testimony of this Wronged One, neither obliteration shall overtake it nor change find its way unto it.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh counselling all to assist the Cause through deeds and character; supplies conduct as the test of the sword image.

selected.text: I swear by the Most Great Name that if a deaf and mute person rises to praise the Truth, he will speak with an eloquent and articulate tongue and, like the nightingale of the garden of divine knowledge, will warble melodies in diverse modes upon the branches and twigs of the Lote-Tree beyond which there is no passing.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that even a deaf and mute person who rises to praise will speak like the nightingale of divine knowledge.

selected.text: When thou hast comprehended what We have mentioned and understood what We have explained, thou wilt recognize the dawning of the Divine Word upon the receptive vessels of creation in the world of the atoms, and thou wilt realize the first blast in the forms of power and the second blast in the realm of simplicity and mercy.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on recognizing the dawning of the Divine Word upon the receptive vessels of creation.

selected.text: The sword is My remembrance and the spearpoint is the tongue. Draw them forth by My leave, then help the All-Merciful through them amidst all worlds. Thus have ye been commanded by the Revealer of verses. By My life! The sword of utterance is sharper than the sword of steel - know this, O ye who are endued with insight!
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh naming His remembrance the sword and the tongue the spearpoint, and declaring the sword of utterance sharper than steel.

selected.text: Praise be to God Who hath manifested through wisdom, revealed His Cause through wisdom, commanded all through wisdom, and made victory to reside in utterance and wisdom. Exalted is the Lord of wisdom and the Manifestor of wisdom, Who hath made it sharper than swords, more penetrating than spears, and more piercing than arrows.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh praising God Who made victory reside in utterance and wisdom, sharper than swords and more piercing than arrows.

selected.text: A word that proceeds from the mine of righteousness and sincerity for God's sake is indeed all-powerful and all-encompassing. When such a word is cast upon a people or an army, they become so enthralled that neither worldly conditions nor all that the nations possess can deter them from the Straight Path and the Momentous News.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh describing a word from the mine of sincerity as all-powerful, holding a people or an army to the Straight Path.

selected.text: It is the cup-bearer of the wine of love and the manifestation of affection and fellowship. The divine Books have appeared through it and their mysteries are inscribed by it. Exalted is He Who hath favored it with that which the writer and His creation are powerless to describe, and taught it and made known to it what He desired.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on the pen as cup-bearer of love through which the divine Books appeared.

selected.text: Aid thy Lord with the sword of utterance - thus hath the matter been decreed from the Pen of the All-Merciful in these days wherein sorrows have encompassed Me from all directions, and God is witness unto this. Know thou that in those days God hath ordained the victory of His Cause through exposition rather than through the tongue
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh calling for aid through the sword of utterance and ordaining victory through exposition.

selected.text: The letters which I sent to you are as the fragrant breezes of the garden of the knowledge of God, which can be smelled by every one whose sense of smelling is clean and purified from any rheum, because they are glad-tidings proceeding from pure lips which are fluent in explaining the mysteries
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá likening His letters to fragrant breezes perceived by those whose sense is purified.

selected.text: When we speak let our speech be an outward evidence of the inner light, for we must speak the truth, otherwise we shall not act wisely. … I hope that you will all become eloquent. The greatest gifts of man are reason and eloquence of expression. The perfect man is both intelligent and eloquent. He has knowledge and knows how to express it
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that speech should be outward evidence of the inner light and that reason and eloquence are the greatest gifts of man.

selected.text: That very mention which flowed from the tongue of that Beloved concerning its dispatch cannot be equaled by anything hidden and treasured in the earth in the estimation of the friends and chosen ones. In truth, love is a sovereign that is mighty and a ruler that prevails. The world of motion and stillness is within the grasp of its power.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh valuing a loving mention above all hidden treasure and calling love a mighty sovereign.

selected.text: in such wise that the tyranny of the oppressors hath failed to deter thee. We behold thee speaking at all times in praise of thy Lord, even after thou wert imprisoned among the silent ones. And We see thee possessed of sight amidst the blind, and standing firm among those who sit. Through thee was raised the shrill voice of every pen and every wise decree was expounded. selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh praising one who spoke God’s praise even when imprisoned among the silent; speech persisting under difficulty.

selected.text: Every power and capacity that is expended in the Cause of God - its effects remain and it yields lasting results. selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in Paris that powers spent for God endure, and that utterance joined with sanctification produces mighty effects.

selected.text: Whoso opens his lips today in remembrance of his Lord will be reinforced by the hosts of God's revelation through wondrous inspiration, and God will cause the Kawthar of divine knowledge to flow from his mouth and will make him speak with wisdom and utterance in such wise that none among all created things shall be able to speak in his presence.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh promising that whoso opens his lips in remembrance will be reinforced and the Kawthar of knowledge will flow from his mouth.

selected.text: thou too must show forth such courage and valor--yet not through the sharp blade and perilous arrow, but rather through a honeyed tongue and sweet utterance and conduct like pure honey and nectar. This sword taketh not life but bestoweth it; it destroyeth not but buildeth up; it casteth not down hearth and home but raiseth up heavenly foundations
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá redefining courage as honeyed speech whose sword bestows life and builds up; the key explanation of the sword image.

selected.text: The spiritual susceptibilities in the hearts are understood by them as 'communication', because between the souls of disincarnated spirits and the embodied, incarnated spirits there exists strong connection and definite and well-established relationship. Those ideal connections are, therefore, the means of receiving and bestowing Divine Favours.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on spiritual susceptibilities as communication between souls; extends the language of the heart.

selected.text: Most would say this kind of speech and utterance and the influence and penetration of His blessed word was extraordinary - that in one gathering the manner of speech and impact of His blessed utterance could satisfy opposing souls and fulfill the ultimate desires of people of different dispositions and aims while also explaining and expressing truth.
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing how His blessed utterance in a single gathering satisfied opposing souls while expressing truth.

selected.text: In truth, the pen is a great sign from the Ancient Lord, and ink is the supreme gate of love and unity. These two have ever been and shall continue to be the movers of the cord of love. Were the favors of God, exalted be His glory, and likewise the effects and fruits ordained for these two to become manifest, the world would be struck with wonderment.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the pen is a great sign and ink the supreme gate of love and unity.

selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh praying for servants who guide through wisdom and utterance and speak what is meet to be spoken.

selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh describing the shrill voice through which souls were drawn nigh and hidden mysteries unveiled.

selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on the fruits of the letter and the resonant soundless pen, source of the world’s sounds; the guide’s soundless-pen passage.

selected.text: What a bounty this is, that the effect of ink seeks the rose of the garden of the heart and perfumes minds - and this is nothing but the bounty of the Ancient Beauty and the Greatest Name, Who has bestowed such grace and granted such power to the musk-scented pen that it gives souls the intoxication of spiritual wine and freely grants eternal joy and expansion to hearts.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on the bounty by which the effect of ink perfumes minds and gives souls spiritual joy.

selected.text: Therefore, O thou who art intoxicated with the wine of the eternal covenant, be assisted to speak and utter in such wise that, like penetrating rays dispersing the clouds of doubt of every wavering soul, thou mayest be as a flash of lightning, becoming a manifestation of divine confirmations, a dawning-place of heavenly assistance, and a rising-point of the lights of unity.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking that speech be like penetrating rays dispersing the clouds of doubt.

selected.text: The words of many speakers are mixed with the lusts of their souls and their worldly appetites; therefore they will have neither authority nor success. … Jesus said: "Arise, take up thy bed and walk." selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá contrasting speech mixed with self and appetite with Christ’s creative word spoken through spiritual authority.

selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to Albert Vail on how a teacher should answer questions about his conduct; a practical instance of considered speech to enquirers.

selected.reason: Suriy-i-Ismuna’l-Mursil passage on a Name made a sun illumining all existence; opens the section on the divine Word.

selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling speech a mirror of the heart and citing Imam ‘Ali that the tongue reveals the hidden man; supplies the guide’s mirror image.

selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that each word of a sincere letter was a messenger of love and that a single word can transform hell into paradise.

selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that one who found the sweetness of the verses would cry out and set the horizons aflame.

Abasement hath reached such a pass that the mute claimeth to have heard the melodies that were raised between earth and
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on abasement that makes the dumb speak and the mute claim to have heard; a paradox of speech and silence.

selected.text: The time of silence hath passed. The day when the Sovereign of Eternity emerged from behind the veils of names and attributes, rent asunder the clouds of knowledge and tore apart the mists of wisdom, and without concealment or veil the Tongue of the Lord of Lords began to speak - in such wise that the oceans of meanings flowed from His blessed lips and the surging waves of utterance streamed forth from His life-giving words.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh declaring that the time of silence has passed and oceans of meaning flow from the Lord’s lips.

selected.text: From the most eloquent tongue We have turned to the luminous tongue. The friends of God must cleave unto wisdom and forbearance, and associate with all the peoples of the world in a spirit of joy and fragrance. In one utterance may be concealed the Water of Life that bestoweth eternal existence, and in another utterance may lie deadly poison. The people of unity must speak with words sweeter than honey and more delicate than the morning dew.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh contrasting the Water of Life and deadly poison in a single utterance and asking for words sweeter than honey.

selected.text: God and oppose not Him Whom all on earth have opposed. Sufficient unto Him is what hath befallen Him and what continueth to befall Him from those who have denied God, the Mighty, the Beloved. And thou, O thou who gazest upon thy Lord's Most Glorious Horizon, hearken unto the melodies of the Dove, then detach thyself from all that hath been created between earth and heaven. Then remind the people of this hidden News, and drink at every moment from the cup of life, though thou didst drink therefrom in the days of thy Lord, to which all things bear witness, yet people hear
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh bidding the reader hearken to the melodies of the Dove and remind the people of the hidden News.

selected.text: Wherefore, O ye beloved of God, offer up thanks that ye have, in the day of the dawning, turned your faces unto the Light of the World and beheld its splendours. Ye have received a share of the light of truth, ye have enjoyed a portion of those blessings that endure forever; and therefore, as a returning of thanks for this bounty, rest ye not for a moment, sit ye not silent, carry to men's ears the glad tidings of the Kingdom, spread far and wide the Word of God.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Among the helpers of God is utterance, both in this Most Great Revelation and formerly. Deeds and goodly character are the hosts of God and are engaged in rendering assistance. If utterance is made with due measure it is God's mercy, but if it exceeds bounds it becomes the cause of destruction. In the Tablets We have counseled all to utter such words as possess the potency and effect of milk, that the children of the world may be nurtured thereby and attain maturity.
selected.reason: Lawh-i-Ittihad passage naming utterance among the helpers of God, merciful in due measure but destructive beyond bounds, and counselling words with the potency of milk.

selected.text: It is said that man is a rational being endowed with the faculty of speech and utterance, that he is aware of universal truths and can perceive mystical and secret meanings. But within the precincts of the Unconstrained, the real purpose of speech among the truly wise is to give praise to the Ancient Beauty and the essence of meaningful utterance is to describe the attributes of the Most Great Name. … Otherwise a dumb animal is better than a human being endowed with speech
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the real purpose of speech among the wise is praise of God, otherwise a dumb animal is better; a substantive account of speech’s purpose.

selected.text: Today is a different day and a different heaven is upraised and a different sea is surging. It cannot and will not be compared with before and after. Say: Today the sun of bounty is manifest and the ocean of grace is before all faces. Move in this spiritual atmosphere with the wings of spirit, and keep yourselves detached, free and sanctified from the impurities, allusions and dust of the vicissitudes of time. Wings soiled with mud are not worthy of flight nor capable of ascension.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that today is a different day; wings soiled with mud cannot fly.

selected.text: The faculty of hearing is more important than the faculty of seeing. Firstly because it is revealed in the Khoran: 'He (God) is the Hearer and the Seer!' We observe that in this verse the word 'Hearer' precedes the word 'Seer'. Secondly 'sight' is a faculty possessed by animals as well as by men, of perceiving only external objects in a direct line, the impressions of which are imprinted on the retina of the eyes while 'hearing' is the faculty or the sense by which sound is perceived from every direction
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explaining why hearing is more important than seeing; gives listening its own substantive place in the guide.

selected.text: A word that is spoken for God's sake contains within it the nature and effect of milk whose taste has not changed, and it will raise the children of the age to the lofty station of maturity and give them to drink from the ocean of knowledge.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that a word spoken for God has the nature of unchanged milk, raising the children of the age to maturity; develops the nourishment image.

selected.text: A myriad names and attributes have been ascribed to these degrees and stations, which I am disinclined to mention here. It is, indeed, solely because of thy longing and devotion that I have engaged in such ephemeral and limited topics. And this, notwithstanding that speech is the greatest evidence of the worth of the speaker and guideth unto the recognition of the source of guidance, for no more complete and enduring proof hath been or will be vouchsafed unto man from the empyrean of everlasting glory than words and utterance.

selected.text: Speak not that which would startle souls, cause flesh to creep, make limbs to tremble, and make the hearts of obstinate people recoil. Rather, speak to them with gentle words that they might remember or fear God. … Follow thou the way of thy Lord, and say not that which the ears cannot bear to hear, for such speech is like luscious food given to small children. However palatable, rare and rich the food may be, it cannot be assimilated by the digestive organs of a suckling child. Therefore unto every one who hath a right, let his settled measure be given

selected.text: Every word is endowed with a spirit, therefore the speaker or expounder should carefully deliver his words at the appropriate time and place, for the impression which each word maketh is clearly evident and perceptible.  The Great Being saith:  One word may be likened unto fire, another unto light, and the influence which both exert is manifest in the world.  Therefore an enlightened man of wisdom should primarily speak with words as mild as milk, that the children of men may be nurtured and edified thereby and may attain the ultimate goal of human existence which is the station of true understanding and nobility
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: We beseech God, blessed and exalted be He, to aid thee to return unto His traces and whatsoever hath appeared from Him. Verily He guideth thee and all upon earth to His straight path. Blessed is the strong one who hath purified his heart with the Kawthar flowing from the spring of My Pen and hath taken the chalice of immortality from the hand of the bounty of his Lord, the Most High, the Most Exalted, and hath drunk before all faces in spite of those who have denied God's proof and His evidence, who have disputed His signs and disbelieved in the blessing of His knowledge which was sent down from the heaven of His mercy that hath encompassed all who are in the heavens and on earth.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh blessing one who purified his heart with the Kawthar of His Pen and drank before all.

selected.text: Thy Name, the Swift, hath made me swifter than lightning; Thy Name, the All-Seeing, hath made me more perceiving than all the worlds; Thy Name, the All-Knowing, hath taught me the knowledge of what was and what shall be; and Thy Name, the All-Informed, hath acquainted me with that which none knoweth save whom Thy knowledge willeth, the knowledge that dominateth all who are in the heavens and on earth. … Despite my inherent baseness, Thou hast made me to excel all standards, and notwithstanding my manifest weakness, Thou hast made me powerful through Thy Name, the Almighty, the Powerful. Through me is broken the back of every mighty one, and through me is exalted both the lowly and the high. Were Thou to loose my reins, I would brandish the spears of utterance, subdue the cities of the earth, and take possession of the hearts of those who wander in the wilderness of heedlessness
selected.reason: Prayer of Bahá’u’lláh describing the powers conferred by the Names, ending with the spears of utterance that take possession of hearts.

selected.text: Turn thy face to the Kingdom of holiness, ascend to the summit of divine address, and open thy tongue. Scatter pearls and gems, bestow musk and ambergris, unlock the fragrant casket of mysteries and expand the breasts of those endowed with understanding. … Perfume the horizons, illumine all regions
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bidding the reader open the tongue, scatter pearls and unlock the casket of mysteries; a rich set of images for teaching.
